P.opening: When something keeps changing, what counts as one thing, and what keeps it the same one? Two answers can disagree, both ways round: at sea, one patch of water meets wave after wave, and one wave keeps moving on into new water. ICW does not make either the real thing and the other a way of talking. Its step-by-step test asks whether the sea's own motion keeps both going, or one is only a grouping the sea does nothing to keep up. The last step is not worked out yet, so no case has passed.

F2.opening: A wave crosses the sea while the water under it only bobs in place. So what is the wave? ICW's answer: it is a higher thing that emerges from the water, steers it, and is more real than water.
F2.readme:
# Identity in Changing Wholes

A wave crosses the sea while the water under it only bobs in place. So what is the wave? ICW's answer: it is a higher thing that emerges from the water, steers it, and is more real than water.

F3.opening: A whole differs within itself without division. In a changing whole, identity can persist in two cross-cutting ways: through what changes; through the change across what changes. Each can hold where the other does not. The whole differs without division; its changing differs without division. One change carries both continuities. That change is cohering. Its order is rhythm.

# Identity in Changing Wholes

When something keeps changing, what counts as one thing, and what keeps it the same one? Two answers can disagree, both ways round: at sea, one patch of water meets wave after wave, and one wave keeps moving on into new water. ICW does not make either the real thing and the other a way of talking. Its step-by-step test asks whether the sea's own motion keeps both going, or one is only a grouping the sea does nothing to keep up. The last step is not worked out yet, so no case has passed.

In short, ICW is about what stays the same when things change. Water and waves each stay the same in their own way. ICW does not pick one as the real thing. Its test is not finished.
